title: What Got You Here Won't Get You There: How Successful People Become Even More Successful
author: Marshall Goldsmith with Mark Reiter
target_audience: Leaders seeking to improve interpersonal effectiveness
Individuals interested in personal and professional growth
Human resources and organizational development specialists
core_themes: Why previous behaviors that led to success may become obstacles
Recognition and management of interpersonal habits that hinder progress
The importance of feedback and self-awareness
Strategies for behavioral change and executive coaching
Humility and willingness to change at the peak of one’s career
primary_purpose: To help high-achieving professionals recognize and overcome the subtle behavioral habits that limit their continued growth and effectiveness, offering practical advice on how to make lasting positive changes and maximize future success.

structure_format.organization: Organized into thematic chapters, including identification of behaviors to change, tools for feedback, and steps for implementing and maintaining behavioral changes

key_concepts_lessons: Success at one level of career does not guarantee ongoing advancement—what worked in the past can be a barrier in the future.
Twenty transactional workplace habits often limit professionals—examples include the need to win, adding too much value, failing to give proper recognition, or withholding information.
Acknowledging and seeking feedback are essential to identifying blind spots.
Change is difficult, especially for successful people; it requires humility and persistence.
Feedforward—a forward-looking feedback process—can be more effective than traditional feedback.
Small behavioral changes, consistently implemented, can have outsized impacts on relationships and leadership effectiveness.
notable_features: Focus on behavioral habits specific to successful executives
Introduction of the Feedforward coaching technique
Case studies drawn from real coaching experiences
Accessible for both business and general audiences
Summarized checklists of 'What to Stop' behaviors
cultural_historical_context: Published in the mid-2000s, the book responded to contemporary workplace challenges, where technical skill is insufficient and interpersonal effectiveness becomes critical with increasing responsibility. Goldsmith’s methods paved the way for the modern era of executive coaching and continuous leadership development.
reception_impact: Widely acclaimed in business and leadership circles
Became a staple in executive coaching literature
Praised for its clarity, memorable concepts, and real-world applicability
Utilized in leadership development and MBA curricula
Inspired further works by Goldsmith and other leadership authors
comparable_titles: Triggers: Creating Behavior That Lasts—Becoming the Person You Want to Be by Marshall Goldsmith
The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People by Stephen R. Covey
Leadership and Self-Deception by The Arbinger Institute
